tasks.prompt: Read this repository and create a source-backed architecture diagram of a Ky HTTP request, starting at ky(input, options) and Ky.create and ending at the returned response or final error. Show instance/default option merging and request construction, the native or configured Fetch boundary and timeout/cancellation control, hooks that can replace or stop work, retry eligibility/delay and beforeRetry, and afterResponse/final error handling. Keep the successful path and the meaningful hook bypass/retry branches easy to follow. Progress reporting, streaming implementation details, and schema validation are outside this request.

Read packages/query-core and create a source-backed architecture diagram of the imperative QueryClient.fetchQuery lifecycle at this checkout, even though that method is marked deprecated. Show option/default handling, the QueryCache and Query ownership boundary, fresh-cache versus fetching decisions, reuse of an ongoing fetch, query-function execution and cancellation, retry/pause/resume control, and success/error state updates through observer and cache notifications. Treat the caller-supplied query function as an external behavior boundary. Framework adapters, mutations, infinite queries, persistence plugins, and garbage-collection policy are outside this request.

Read this repository and create a source-backed architecture diagram of a PQueue task from add() to completion or rejection. Show the PQueue controller, waiting priority queue and admission checks for concurrency/interval limits, the caller task execution boundary, how completion releases capacity and starts more work, pause/start, and the different effects of aborting a waiting versus running task and of execution timeout. Distinguish queued work from active work. Strict sliding-window internals, metrics/waiter APIs, and priority-update implementation details are outside this request.
